title: LLM Knowledge Bases: a practical guide — Ben Holmes, Warp
talk_summary: Ben Holmes describes a personal note-taking pipeline where an 'enrich note' agent skill adds tags, source URLs, timestamps, and backlinks to raw markdown notes, then scheduled cloud sandboxes regenerate wikis and HTML graph views overnight. The transferable core is idempotent, timestamp-gated batch enrichment of a markdown corpus by a cheap model, run on a cadence in an ephemeral sandbox.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each note gets an 'enriched at' timestamp written into the file; the batch skill only processes notes lacking that marker, so re-runs are idempotent and cheap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Put a little time stamp on there so if we ask the agent to do another pass it remembers that some other agent did it in the past.

takeaways.what_they_do: All allowed tags live in a reference folder the agent must read; the skill explicitly tells the model to be reluctant to invent new ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I actually instruct the agent to be reluctant to add new tags because Claude loves to get creative.

takeaways.technique: Sync-in / run / sync-out ephemeral sandbox for batch jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: A scheduled cloud sandbox pulls the markdown folder (via Obsidian headless CLI or git clone), runs the skill, and pushes results back, so the laptop need not be open.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we create an automation that takes our folder of markdown syncs it into a box maybe like a cloud sandbox ... and then sync it back up when the agent's done

takeaways.technique: Cadence-scheduled background jobs instead of on-demand
takeaways.what_they_do: Enrichment and wiki regeneration run on daily/weekly schedules so results are ready before the human looks, rather than blocking on a manual invocation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ideally we have a flow that will sort of do this in the background for us. maybe while we sleep, maybe on an automated schedule

takeaways.technique: Agent-generated HTML/graph views over a corpus
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of reading many files, an agent builds a clickable HTML graph of notes and links so a human can spot clusters and gaps at a glance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I told an agent, build this for me. So you can do that now.

takeaways.technique: Cheap open-weight model for bulk enrichment
takeaways.what_they_do: Speaker notes GLM-class open-weight models are 'very good at this sort of task' for bulk note enrichment, reserving stronger models for harder work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you've ever been wanting to experiment with like GLM 5.2, too, just very good at this sort of task
